To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The likelihood ratio-like statistics can be approximated using saddlepoint approximations in permutation tests.

the saddlepoint approximation to the likelihood ratio-like test statistics can be used to construct permutation tests for both $k$-sample and two sample multivariate problems, and that these statistics are more accurate than the classical statistics in many situations.

(i) we extend the use of the saddlepoint approximation for likelihood ratio-like test statistics to permutation tests, (ii) the resulting test statistics have higher power than the classical statistics in the $k$-sample case, (iii) the resulting test statistic is a natural extension of the two-sample case to the multivariate case, (iv) the saddlepoint approximation is a useful alternative to the bootstrap in this context, and (v) the resulting tests are easy to compute.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of approximating the distribution of a likelihood ratio like statistic in a permutation test.
the use of saddlepoint methods in the context of permutation tests.
the problem of approximating the distribution of the likelihood ratio statistic for a given hypothesis when the distribution of the observations is unknown.

the likelihood ratio-like tests are uniformly better than their competitors in all respects.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in some cases the likelihood ratio test can be used as a permutation test, and that the saddlepoint approximation to the distribution of the likelihood ratio test statistic can be used in place of the exact distribution in a permutation test, with the same asymptotic properties.
in some cases the likelihood ratio-like test statistics can be used to obtain permutation tests that are as accurate as the corresponding classical tests.
